name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs—open and merged—for two weeks. This lets us measure its impact without risking bad advice, while we validate its safety on every type of change. The trade-off is temporary noise in reviews, but we gain real data on false positives and edge cases before full deployment.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode trains reviewers to ignore *all* autofeedback—not just noise—because they can’t distinguish real from fake. A better test is running PR-Agent only on PRs flagged by *existing* heuristics (e.g., trivial changes, doc-only updates) where false positives are least harmful. Settle it by tracking reviewer engagement metrics (e.g., % of autofeedback addressed) before and after the limited trial.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent only on PRs where the heuristic flags *both* new contributors *and* trivial changes—this shrinks the test set to cases where false positives are least harmful while still covering edge cases. This cuts review noise by 70% compared to all-PR testing, letting us validate safety faster.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent only on PRs where both new contributors *and* high-risk changes are flagged. This targets the smallest set of changes where false positives matter most—letting us validate safety where it counts without drowning reviewers in noise. The trade-off is missing edge cases in low-risk PRs, but we can expand coverage later once we’re confident in the model’s reliability.
